summary: Kurt Andrew Johnson is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of York by 2010 under the supervision of Jane Moody.

Kurt Huber (1893–1943) was a philosopher who attended Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium and earned his PhD (~1913–1917) and Habilitation (~1917–1920) at the University of Munich. He served there as außerordentlicher Professor (1926) and held a professorship (1938).

Kurt Tropper works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna by 2001 under Ernst Steinkellner, also studying under Michael Torsten Much and Tashi Geisler, and held posts at Vienna and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies Kurtis R. Schaeffer earned his MA at the University of Washington and PhD at Harvard (~1995–2000). He held faculty posts at the University of Alabama (2000, 2004) before becoming professor at the University of Virginia in 2005.
Kurunegoda Piyatissa (1928–2015) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as the head of the New York Buddhist Vihara, where his presence is attested in 1998 and 2009.

Kwangsoo Park specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned an MA from the University of Iowa and a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, later serving as a professor at Wonkwang University (attested 2020).

Scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies Kyo Kano studied at Keio University, Kyoto University, and the University of Vienna. Kano served as an assistant at Kyoto University (attested 1989) and associate professor at Kobe Women's University (attested 2000).

Kyojun Shimizutani (1891–1979) was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Tendai Sect University and Taisho University. He served as professor at Tendai Sect University (1919) and Taisho University (1926–1945), and as head priest at Sensō-ji (~1952–1979).

Kyoko Fujii (born 1948) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. She held professorships at Yokohama City University (1990), Hamamatsu University (1996), Hokkaido University (~1999–2011), and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2011–2019).

Kyoko Tokuno (born 1944) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She held an academic post at the University of Oregon and served as a professor at the University of Washington (attested 2017).

Kyokuga Saeki (1828–1891) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under numerous traditional teachers, including Gen'yu and Reiga. He later served as the 143rd elder of Sennyu-ji from around 1888 to 1891.

Kyosho Hayashima (1920–1987) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts as lecturer at Yokohama City University (1962), assistant professor at Toyo University (1962), and professor at the University of Tokyo (attested 1980).
Kyosho Tanaka (born 1947) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1966 to 1974. He served as an associate professor at Musashino University from ~1975 to 2017.
Kyoshun Todo (1916–1989) was a scholar of Buddhist studies who held positions at Bukkyo University, serving as assistant professor (attested 1962) and later as professor (attested 1988–1992).

Kyozan Joshu Sasaki (1907–2014) was a Buddhist master who studied at Zuiryo-ji and Myoshin-ji under Joten Soko Miura. He served as abbot of Yotoku-in (1947–1953), Shojuan (1953), and Mount Baldy Zen Center (~1971–2012), which he founded.
Kōdō Yamada (1868–1947) was a scholar of Buddhist studies who taught at Komazawa University and Keio University.
Kōichi Kozaka (born 1948) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Hakuyu Hadano. He served as a professor at Osaka Kyoiku University (attested 1991).

Kōun Yamada (1907–1989) was a Buddhist studies and religious figure educated at the First Higher School and University of Tokyo. He studied under traditional teachers including Hakuun Ryōko Yasutani, founded Kamakura Haku-un-kai (1953), and became head of Sanbo Zen (1970).

Kōzen Shaku (1849–1924) was an Indology and Buddhist studies figure who studied under Senmyō. He served as head priest at Gyokuri-ji (1870–1881) and Sange-ji (1882), taught at Nagano Prefectural Northern Chugakurin (1881), and founded Shakuson Shofukai (1893).

Kōzui Ōtani (1876–1948) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Central Asian studies, and archaeology. He studied at Gakushuin and under Eun Maeda, became a fellow of the Royal Geographical Society (~1902), and served as 22nd Abbot of Nishi Hongan-ji (1903–1914).
